158	08 00 00 00              namesz = 8
159	08 00 00 00              descsz = 8
160	01 00 00 00              type   = NT_MINIXRS_IDENT
161	6d 69 6e 69 78 72 73 00  "minixrs\0"
162	01 00 00 00              abi_version = 1
163	00 00 00 00              flags = 0
164	```
165	
166	A linker script consuming this libc must `KEEP()` the section and give it a
167	dedicated `PT_NOTE` at the start of the read-only `PT_LOAD`. Regressing the

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
# Copyright (c) 2025-2026 Kevin Barnard and minix.rs Contributors
#
# Build the musl fork (external/musl) into a cached sysroot at
# target/musl-sysroot (phase-5 decision D10).
#
# Everything this writes lives under target/. The submodule work tree is left
# PRISTINE -- the c-headers CI job asserts a clean `git status`, and a build
# that dirties a submodule would fail it. musl supports out-of-tree builds, so
# the object tree goes to target/musl-build.
#
# Rebuilds are skipped when target/musl-sysroot/.stamp already matches the
# submodule SHA and the toolchain. Pass --force to rebuild anyway.
#
# Environment:
#   MUSL_SRC   musl source tree (default: external/musl). Point this at a local
#              fork checkout to test a port change before bumping the submodule.

set -eu

ROOT=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")/.." && pwd)
MUSL_SRC=${MUSL_SRC:-$ROOT/external/musl}

content.content: Updated task #3 status
Updated task #6 status

1	/*
2	 * minix.rs user-space linker script (aarch64 EL0 worker — the slice-4.7 exec
3	 * target).
4	 *
5	 * Like the server `user.ld`: a static ET_EXEC ELF the kernel's minimal loader
6	 * (`kernel/src/boot_image/elf.rs`) maps segment-by-segment into a fresh
7	 * per-process AddrSpace. Every PT_LOAD is page-aligned (vaddr *and* file
8	 * offset); no dynamic sections / relocations.
9	 *
10	 * One deliberate difference (slice 5.5): the text segment carries FILEHDR and
11	 * PHDRS, and `.` starts at SIZEOF_HEADERS above the load base, so PT_LOAD #0
12	 * begins at file offset 0 and covers the ELF header + program headers. Without
13	 * that, lld's default aarch64 max-page-size (64 KiB) puts the first PT_LOAD at
14	 * offset 0x10000 and leaves `e_phoff` in an unmapped prefix — so `SYS_EXEC`
15	 * would have no mapped VA to report as AT_PHDR, and musl's `__init_tls` (which
16	 * walks the headers from there) would have nothing to walk. The segment start
17	 * stays page-aligned in both vaddr and offset, so the loader's strict checks are
18	 * unaffected; only the entry moves up one page. Server scripts are NOT changed:
19	 * boot-loaded images get no initial stack frame and never read an auxv.
20	 *
21	 * Load base 0x0010_0000 (1 MiB): the same base servers use — the worker only
22	 * ever runs after `SYS_EXEC` builds it its own per-process TTBR0, so the shared
23	 * base never collides. The stack is NOT part of the ELF: exec allocates a stack
24	 * frame and sets SP_EL0 before eret.
25	 */
26	
27	OUTPUT_FORMAT(elf64-littleaarch64)
28	OUTPUT_ARCH(aarch64)
29	ENTRY(_start)
30	
31	PHDRS {
32	    text   PT_LOAD FILEHDR PHDRS FLAGS(5); /* R+X */
33	    rodata PT_LOAD FLAGS(4); /* R   */
34	    data   PT_LOAD FLAGS(6); /* RW  */
35	    note   PT_NOTE FLAGS(4); /* minixrs identity note */
36	}
37	
38	SECTIONS {
39	    . = 0x00100000 + SIZEOF_HEADERS;
40	
41	    .text : ALIGN(4K) {
42	        KEEP(*(.text._start))
43	        *(.text .text.*)
44	    } :text
45	
46	    . = ALIGN(4K);
47	    /*
48	     * minixrs identity note (tooling/docs/abi-note.md): first thing in the
49	     * RO segment, dual-assigned so it lands in the rodata PT_LOAD *and* its
50	     * own PT_NOTE phdr. KEEP() is mandatory — nothing references the
51	     * section — and this rule must stay ahead of the /DISCARD/ *(.note.*)
52	     * rule below (first match wins).
53	     */
54	    .note.minixrs.ident : {
55	        KEEP(*(.note.minixrs.ident))
56	    } :rodata :note
57	
58	    .rodata : {
59	        *(.rodata .rodata.*)
60	    } :rodata
61	
62	    . = ALIGN(4K);
63	    .data : ALIGN(4K) {
64	        *(.data .data.*)
65	    } :data
66	
67	    .bss : ALIGN(4K) {
68	        *(.bss .bss.*)
69	        *(COMMON)
70	    } :data
71	
72	    /DISCARD/ : {
73	        *(.eh_frame)
74	        *(.eh_frame_hdr)
75	        *(.note .note.*)
76	        *(.comment)
77	        *(.dynsym .dynstr .hash .gnu.hash .dynamic)
78	    }
79	}

content.text: v1.2.6's `fmt_fp` uses a **VLA** (`uint32_t big[bufsize]`), so the big allocation is runtime-computed and invisible to a static scan. Computing it: `%Lf` would need ~7.4 KB, `%f` ~512 B — but `hello.c` prints no floats, so `fmt_fp` is never called. Measured worst chain is ~2 KB. Let me wire it into the build and test empirically:

# first PT_LOAD covers the ELF header. Revert that link change and this becomes
# auxv=1: the count is what makes the conditional arm observable rather than
# quietly dead. sp is last because it is the run-variable field.
[exec] argc=1 envc=0 auxv=4 sp=0x

# ...and the EL0 half, which is the one that actually proves anything: the trace
# above only says the kernel *thinks* it wrote a frame. `worker`'s _start is
# naked (`mov x0, sp` is the first instruction it runs, so no prologue can
# perturb the value) and it checks the frame byte for byte -- alignment, argc,
# the argv[0] string, both NULL terminators, AT_PAGESZ, and a phdr readable at
# AT_PHDR. The verdict leaves as its exit status rather than a console line,
# because worker runs once per init fork cycle; init reaps that child -- matched
# by pid, since PM parents the demo stubs to init and stub D's early SIGSEGV
# would otherwise be the first thing reaped -- and prints its status once. A
# failing check turns this into `exec stack FAIL code=N` (forbidden), naming
# which property broke. Success is the positive sentinel EXEC_STACK_PROBE_PASS,
# not 0: PM's kill path zombifies a signalled process without setting
# exit_status, so a worker that faulted before reporting is reaped with 0 --
# which prints `exec stack FAIL no-verdict` rather than passing silently.
minix.rs init: exec stack ok

# produced before slice 5.1's PT-walk copy engine. `!!! KERNEL PANIC:` catches
# it transitively (exception_entry panics), but this is the sharper canary for
# exactly the regression that slice prevents, and it can never appear in a
# healthy boot.
!!! kernel exception (vector index
!!! unexpected EL0 sync exception
!!! EL0 instruction abort
!!! EL0 data abort

# Slice 5.5: the exec initial stack failed its EL0 check. Both spellings are
# listed because they fail independently: worker writes its own line straight to
# fd 2 (belt and braces, in case the exit-status path is what broke), and init
# prints the reaped verdict with the number of the first failing check. Either
# one appearing means a process is being handed a frame musl's crt could not
# read -- and neither can appear in a healthy boot.

minix.rs init: exec stack FAIL

# VFS answers EBADF for fd 3 (in range of the fd row, not open), the driver
# relays it, syscall_ret.c turns the negative return into errno, and the value C
# compares against <errno.h>'s EBADF matches. Emitted ONLY when write(3, ...)
# returns -1 *and* errno == EBADF, so it cannot appear by accident.

3	// Assembles the per-arch entry path and exception vectors into the kernel.
4	//
5	// .S files go through clang (cross-targeted at the kernel triple) and the
6	// resulting .o files are passed straight to the linker via cargo:rustc-link-arg.
7	// We deliberately *avoid* the cc crate's static-library packaging because the
8	// linker's archive member resolution wouldn't pull in `_start` (it's only
9	// referenced via the linker-script `ENTRY` directive, not from any Rust
10	// symbol). Direct .o linkage sidesteps that, and it also dodges the
11	// macOS-ar/ELF-object mismatch entirely.
12	
13	use std::path::PathBuf;
14	use std::process::Command;
15	
16	fn main() {
17	    // The kernel is bare-metal only. It used to collapse to a no-op `main` on
18	    // host targets so `cargo check --workspace` stayed green, at the cost of
19	    // hiding every module behind `#[cfg(target_os = "none")]` — and therefore
20	    // from every lint gate.
21	    //
22	    // `forced-target` in Cargo.toml now pins this package to
23	    // aarch64-unknown-none for *every* cargo invocation, so in practice this
24	    // arm is unreachable. It stays as defense-in-depth: if that unstable
25	    // feature is ever dropped, this turns a cascade of `no_main` /
26	    // unset-`BOOT_IMAGE_PATH` errors into one actionable message, and it fires
27	    // before rustc runs.
28	    let target_os = std::env::var("CARGO_CFG_TARGET_OS").unwrap_or_default();
29	    if target_os != "none" {
30	        println!(

32	             cannot be built for the host (got target_os = \"{target_os}\"). Build it with \
33	             `cargo kernel-aarch64`. If you are seeing this at all, the `forced-target` key \
34	             in kernel/Cargo.toml is not taking effect — check that cargo still supports the \
35	             unstable `per-package-target` feature."
36	        );
37	        return;
38	    }
39	
40	    let arch = std::env::var("CARGO_CFG_TARGET_ARCH").expect("CARGO_CFG_TARGET_ARCH unset");
41	    let out_dir = PathBuf::from(std::env::var_os("OUT_DIR").expect("OUT_DIR unset"));
42	
43	    // The `boot-stubs` feature (default-on) gates the demo stubs A–D. Build
44	    // scripts can't see `#[cfg(feature = ...)]`, so read the env var cargo sets
45	    // for enabled features. Off ⇒ skip `user_stub.S` assembly and build PM
46	    // stub-free so the two crates agree on `NR_STUB_PROCS`.
47	    let stubs = std::env::var_os("CARGO_FEATURE_BOOT_STUBS").is_some();
48

50	        "aarch64" => {
51	            let mut sources = vec![
52	                "src/arch/aarch64/entry.S",
53	                "src/arch/aarch64/vectors.S",
54	                "src/arch/aarch64/trap.S",

71	                        "-c",

# external/ — vendored third-party code

Two different vendoring mechanisms live here, for two different reasons.

| Directory | Mechanism | Upstream | Licence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `limine/` | `make` fetch of a pinned commit (artifacts gitignored) | [limine-bootloader/limine](https://github.com/limine-bootloader/limine) | BSD Zero Clause |
| `musl/` | git submodule, pinned commit on branch `minixrs` | [minixrs/musl-minixrs](https://github.com/minixrs/musl-minixrs) | MIT |

See `limine/README.md` for the bootloader. The rest of this file covers musl.

## `musl/` — the libc fork (slice 5.6)

`external/musl` is a submodule of **`minixrs/musl-minixrs`**, our fork of
[musl libc](https://musl.libc.org/), tracking its **`minixrs`** branch — *not*
`main`, which is a pristine upstream mirror with no port on it. The fork is
based on upstream tag `v1.2.6`.

musl is **MIT licensed**; the fork adds nothing under a different licence. This
table is the only record of that fact in this repo: `cargo-deny` and
`cargo-audit` walk the cargo dependency graph, which a C source tree is invisible
to, so nothing automated can notice the licence here.

Initialise it with:

```sh
git submodule update --init --recursive
```

### Building it

`tools/build-musl.sh` drives configure/make into a cached sysroot at
`target/musl-sysroot`. Everything it writes lives under `target/`; the submodule
work tree is left **pristine**, because the `c-headers` CI job asserts a clean
`git status` and a build that dirtied a submodule would fail it.

Nothing builds musl automatically. `kernel/build.rs` presence-checks
`target/musl-sysroot/.stamp` and, when it is missing or stale, packs the
`worker` ELF under the name `hello` and emits a `cargo::warning` — so a fresh
clone still boots green, it just loses the slice-5.6 C markers. Kicking off a
multi-minute libc build from inside a cargo build script would be worse.

### Bumping the pin

The port branch is **force-pushed** when it is rebased onto a new upstream tag,
which orphans whatever commit this submodule pins. So a fork rebase and the
submodule bump here must land in the **same PR** — otherwise this repo points at
a commit that no longer exists and the submodule fails to clone.

The fork's own `MINIXRS.md` carries the branch contract, the delta contract, and
a Linux-dependency inventory re-derived against v1.2.6.

# The C toolchain and the musl port

Slice 5.6 is Phase 5's **milestone A**: an ordinary C program, compiled against
a forked musl and linked with `rust-lld`, running on minix.rs with `printf`
reaching the serial console.

Nothing in that program is minix.rs-specific — it is plain C against plain
`<stdio.h>`. It works because the libc underneath it was ported, not because the
program was. That is the whole point of the exercise.

```c
printf("minix.rs hello: Hello from C!\n");
```

```
minix.rs hello: Hello from C!
```

## Where the pieces live

| Piece | Location |
|---|---|
| The libc fork | `external/musl` (submodule → `minixrs/musl-minixrs`, branch `minixrs`) |
| Sysroot builder | `tools/build-musl.sh` → `target/musl-sysroot` |
| The C program | `userland/hello/{hello.c,hello.ld}` |
| Compile + link | `kernel/build.rs`'s `build_hello` |
| Generated ABI headers | `cargo gen-c-headers` → `target/gen-c-headers/include/minixrs/` |

## The seam: Linux syscall numbers in, IPC out

minix.rs has no Linux syscall ABI. Its only `svc #0` entry point is the MINIX
IPC trap, and every OS service is a user-space server reached by message
passing. Yet musl is written throughout in terms of `__syscall(SYS_write, …)`.

The port resolves this in **one file**. `arch/aarch64/syscall_arch.h` normally
executes `svc` with the syscall number in `x8`; in the fork, every `__syscallN`
instead calls `__minixrs_syscall`, which switches on the Linux number and issues
the corresponding server round-trip:

| Linux syscall | minix.rs mapping |
|---|---|
| `writev` | one `VFS_WRITE` per iovec, counts summed |
| `write` | one `VFS_WRITE` |
| `exit_group`, `exit` | `PM_EXIT` (does not return) |
| `set_tid_address` | constant tid `1` |
| `ioctl` | `-ENOTTY` |
| everything else | `-ENOSYS` |

Keeping musl's ~297 call sites unmodified is what lets the other ~1900 source
files stay byte-identical to upstream — and therefore rebase for free onto the
next release. The **entire** fork delta is `arch/aarch64/syscall_arch.h`,
`src/minixrs/`, a brand block in `crt/crt1.c`, and a `MINIXRS.md`.

Six syscalls is enough only because musl's startup path avoids the rest: with
`AT_UID`/`AT_GID`/`AT_SECURE` absent from the auxv, `__init_libc` takes an early
return that skips its `ppoll`; `__init_ssp(NULL)` derives the stack canary
arithmetically; and `__init_tls` uses its static `builtin_tls` because the
program has no `PT_TLS`. The fork's `MINIXRS.md` records each of those facts,
re-derived against v1.2.6 rather than assumed.

### `ioctl` is load-bearing

Answering `-ENOTTY` is not merely harmless. `__stdout_write` sets `f->lbf = -1`
when `TIOCGWINSZ` fails, which makes stdout **fully buffered** — so `printf`
output does not appear when it is called, but when `exit()` runs `__stdio_exit`.
A boot log containing `Hello from C!` therefore proves the flush path too, not
just formatting.

## What a `write` actually does

```
hello.c   printf(…)
musl      vfprintf → __stdio_write → __syscall(SYS_writev, …)
fork      __minixrs_syscall → VFS_WRITE (SENDREC to VFS)
VFS       issues a CPF_MAGIC grant over the caller's buffer → CDEV_WRITE
TTY       SYS_SAFECOPY pulls the bytes in, writes the PL011
```

The buffer never leaves the caller's address space until the driver copies it,
and it moves in exactly **one** copy. VFS names the grant's owner from the
kernel-stamped `m_source`, never from the payload — a caller-supplied owner
would turn VFS into a confused deputy, since VFS holds `SYS_PROC` and its
clients do not.

## Building

```sh
tools/build-musl.sh     # configure + make into target/musl-sysroot
cargo kernel-aarch64    # build.rs compiles and links userland/hello
```

The sysroot build uses `clang --target=aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` with `AR` and
`RANLIB` from the pinned Rust toolchain (`llvm-ar`, and `llvm-ar s` in place of
`llvm-ranlib`, which that toolchain does not ship). Linking uses `rust-lld` —
no platform linker and no Homebrew LLVM anywhere in the path.

`build-musl.sh` also runs the **real** errno check that slice 5.0 deferred to
here: it compiles the generated `<minixrs/errno.h>`'s opt-in POSIX block against
the fork's own `bits/errno.h`, so a POSIX errno whose magnitude drifted from
musl's is a build failure. Until this slice, CI could only prove macro
spellings.

### If the sysroot is missing

`kernel/build.rs` presence-checks `target/musl-sysroot/.stamp`. When it is
absent or stale it emits a `cargo::warning` and packs the `worker` ELF **under
the name `hello`**, so a fresh clone still boots green and only the
hello-specific markers go missing. It deliberately does not build the sysroot
itself — a multi-minute libc build launched from a cargo build script would turn
a first `cargo kernel-aarch64` into a mystery.

## `hello.ld`

The linker script starts from `userland/worker/user.ld` and keeps the parts that
are load-bearing there: page-aligned `PT_LOAD`s, no dynamic sections, a 1 MiB
load base, and the `FILEHDR PHDRS` idiom that puts `PT_LOAD` #0 at file offset
`0`. That idiom is **mandatory** here rather than merely nice: without it lld's
default 64 KiB page size leaves `e_phoff` in an unmapped prefix, and musl's
`__init_tls` walks the program headers from exactly the `AT_PHDR` the kernel
reports.

What it adds is everything a musl link brings that a Rust one does not, all of
it from `crti.o` / `crtn.o` / `libc.a`: `.init` and `.fini` (which define the
`_init`/`_fini` that `crt1.c` hands to `__libc_start_main`), `.init_array` /
`.fini_array` with their bracketing symbols, `.got`, and `.data.rel.ro`. Every
input section gets an explicit home, because an orphan placed past the last
`PT_LOAD` is a **silent** load failure — the kernel maps what the program
headers describe and never sees it.

Verify any change with:

```sh
"$(rustc --print sysroot)"/lib/rustlib/*/bin/llvm-readobj --program-headers \
  --elf-output-style=GNU target/hello/hello
```

## Quad-float builtins

musl's `vfprintf` references soft-float `binary128` helpers (`__multf3`,
`__floatsitf`, …): aarch64's `long double` is IEEE quad with no hardware
support. musl's `configure` finds no runtime library on this host, so those
symbols would be undefined at link time.

They come from the pinned toolchain's own `compiler_builtins`, built for the
custom `aarch64-unknown-minixrs` target by the server builds that run first.
Note that the *prebuilt* `aarch64-unknown-none` rlib in the rustup sysroot does
**not** export the C-ABI names — only the `-Zbuild-std` one does.

## The ELF brand

The kernel refuses to load an unbranded ELF. For Rust binaries the 28-byte
`.note.minixrs.ident` note comes from `minixrs_abi_note::brand!()`; for C it is
emitted from `crt/crt1.c` as a `.pushsection` global asm, so every C program is
branded with no opt-in. `crt1.o` is linked explicitly rather than pulled from an
archive, so — unlike a `libc.a` member — it can never be dropped by
archive-member selection.

Regressing it fails the **kernel build**, not the boot: `kernel/build.rs` runs
the same `scan_brand` check when it packs the boot archive.

## The ABI freeze

Slice 5.6 is the ABI freeze point (phase-5 decision D8). There is now C that
depends on the message layout, the call numbers, the endpoint encoding, and the
errno values, and it lives in a **different repository**. Past this slice those
change only via a deliberate ABI-bump PR touching both repos together.

`.note.minixrs.ident` note comes from `minixrs_abi_note::brand!()`; for C it is
emitted from `crt/crt1.c` as a `.pushsection` global asm, so every C program is
branded with no opt-in. `crt1.o` is linked explicitly rather than pulled from an
archive, so — unlike a `libc.a` member — it can never be dropped by
archive-member selection.

Regressing it fails the **kernel build**, not the boot: `kernel/build.rs` runs
the same `scan_brand` check when it packs the boot archive.

## The ABI freeze

Slice 5.6 is the ABI freeze point (phase-5 decision D8). There is now C that
depends on the message layout, the call numbers, the endpoint encoding, and the
errno values, and it lives in a **different repository**. Past this slice those
change only via a deliberate ABI-bump PR touching both repos together.

**Proof (milestone A):** `printf("Hello from C on minix.rs!\n")` output
reaches serial through VFS→TTY from a musl-linked binary exec'd out of the
MXBI archive; marker in `qemu-boot.expected`.

**As built** — deltas from the scope above:

- **The fork was recreated, not reused.** The old `KevinBarnard/musl-minix`
  (v1.2.5 + 103 commits, a stray `CLAUDE.md` on its working branch) is
  **archived**; the port lives in a fresh `minixrs/musl-minixrs` pushed from a
  clean clone of `git.musl-libc.org`, with `main` = pristine upstream mirror and
  `minixrs` (the default branch) = the port, based on tag **`v1.2.6`**
  (2026-03-20). The v1.2.5 `linux-inventory.md` was **not** carried over — it was
  re-derived against v1.2.6 into the fork's `MINIXRS.md`, which also carries the
  branch and delta contracts.
- **Split 5.6a (fork) / 5.6b (this repo)**, the 4.6a/4.6b precedent, per the
  cross-repo rule.
- **`minix` → `minixrs` throughout**, since 5.6 is the ABI freeze and this was
  the last cheap moment: `src/minixrs/` and `__minixrs_syscall` in the fork, and
  on this side the generated C surface too — `include/minixrs/*.h`,
  `_MINIXRS_OFFSETOF`, `MINIXRS_ABI_CHECK_POSIX_ERRNO`. Prose citing *MINIX 3's*
  own headers (`callnr_h.rs`'s deviation note, `com_h.rs`'s `<minix/const.h>`)
  was deliberately left alone. The `minix-ipc/` **directory** was renamed
  `minixrs-ipc/` to match its long-standing package name.
- **`PM_EXEC` gained a 16-byte name payload** (`PM_EXEC_NAME_OFF`), replacing
  PM's hardcoded `EXEC_TARGET`, and **init alternates `worker` / `hello`**
  (`EXEC_TARGETS`) rather than flipping outright — the written scope's "flips
  `worker` → `hello`" predates 5.5 making `worker` the exec-stack probe, and
  flipping would have retired `[exec] … auxv=4` and `init: exec stack ok`.
  Groundwork 5.9's path form needs anyway. Reading the name uses a new
  host-tested `server-rt::payload::rd_name`.
- **The fallback presence-checks the SYSROOT, not the submodule**
  (`target/musl-sysroot/.stamp`). Checking the submodule would let a fresh clone
  that ran `git submodule update` but not `tools/build-musl.sh` trigger a
  multi-minute libc build from inside a cargo build script.
- **`RANLIB` is `llvm-ar s`, not `llvm-ranlib`** — the pinned toolchain ships
  `llvm-ar` but not `llvm-ranlib`.
- **Quad-float builtins had to be sourced.** musl's `vfprintf` references
  `__multf3` / `__floatsitf` / … (aarch64 `long double` is IEEE quad, no
  hardware support) and musl's configure finds no runtime library on this host.

input.old_string: General rule for any probe reporting through an exit status: **encode the pass, never the absence of a failure**
input.new_string:
General rule for any probe reporting through an exit status: **encode the pass, never the absence of a failure**

- **C on minix.rs — the musl port, the sysroot, and the ABI freeze (slice 5.6, milestone A):** the libc is a **git submodule at `external/musl`** → `minixrs/musl-minixrs`, tracking branch **`minixrs`** (the port; `main` is a pristine upstream mirror with nothing on it), based on tag **`v1.2.6`**. The old `KevinBarnard/musl-minix` is archived and nothing was carried over. The fork's whole delta is `arch/aarch64/syscall_arch.h` + `src/minixrs/` + a brand block in `crt/crt1.c` + `MINIXRS.md`, and staying that small is the design goal — **musl globs `src/*/`, so `src/minixrs/` needs no Makefile edit**. Every `__syscallN` calls `__minixrs_syscall`, which switches on the *Linux* number musl still emits and issues a server round-trip (`writev`/`write` → `VFS_WRITE`, `exit`/`exit_group` → `PM_EXIT`, `set_tid_address` → 1, `ioctl` → `-ENOTTY`, everything else `-ENOSYS`); musl's ~297 call sites stay untouched, which is what lets ~1900 files rebase for free. `syscall_ret.c` is untouched because D7's magnitudes (`1..=40`, `>=200`) all sit inside its `> -4096UL` window. **`ioctl` → `-ENOTTY` is load-bearing**: it makes `__stdout_write` set `f->lbf = -1`, so stdout is **fully buffered** and `printf` only reaches the console via `exit()`'s `__stdio_exit` — the milestone marker therefore proves the flush path too. Six syscalls suffice only because of startup facts that must be **re-verified, never assumed, on any musl bump** (all re-read against v1.2.6, recorded in the fork's `MINIXRS.md`): `__init_libc` early-returns past its `ppoll` when `AT_UID`/`AT_GID`/`AT_SECURE` are absent (they read 0); `__init_ssp(NULL)` derives the canary arithmetically; `__init_tp`'s only syscall is `set_tid_address` (`__set_thread_area` is `msr tpidr_el0` inline asm since v1.2.6) and it **walks `libc.auxv`**, so the auxv must stay `AT_NULL`-terminated; `__init_tls` uses static `builtin_tls` absent a `PT_TLS` (so no `mmap`) and walks 5.5's `AT_PHDR`/`AT_PHNUM`/`AT_PHENT`. **`tools/build-musl.sh`** builds an out-of-tree sysroot into `target/musl-sysroot` (the submodule work tree stays **pristine** — the `c-headers` job asserts a clean `git status`), keyed by a `.stamp` of submodule SHA + toolchain; `RANLIB` is **`llvm-ar s`**, because the pinned toolchain ships `llvm-ar` but **not `llvm-ranlib``**. It also runs the **real D7 errno *value* check** 5.0 deferred here — the opt-in POSIX block compiled against the fork's own `bits/errno.h` under `-nostdinc -isystem <sysroot>/include`; the CI `c-headers` job keeps only the hermetic stand-in check. `userland/hello` is **not a cargo crate** — `hello.c` + `hello.ld` compiled by clang and linked by `rust-lld` inside `kernel/build.rs::build_hello`, packed under proc_nr `-1` like `worker`. **The fallback presence-checks the SYSROOT (`.stamp`), not the submodule**, and packs the `worker` ELF *under the name* `hello` with a `cargo::warning` — checking the submodule would let a fresh clone trigger a multi-minute libc build from inside a build script. musl's `vfprintf` needs soft-float **binary128** builtins (`__multf3`/`__floatsitf`/…; aarch64 `long double` is IEEE quad) which musl's configure finds no library for: they come from **`compiler_builtins` as built by `-Zbuild-std` for `aarch64-unknown-minixrs`** — the *prebuilt* `aarch64-unknown-none` rlib in the rustup sysroot does **not** export the C-ABI names, so glob the nested target dir, never the sysroot. `hello.ld` is `worker/user.ld` plus what only a musl link brings — `.init`/`.fini` (they define the `_init`/`_fini` `crt1.c` passes to `__libc_start_main`), `.init_array`/`.fini_array` with bracketing symbols, `.got`, `.data.rel.ro` — because **an orphan section past the last `PT_LOAD` is a silent load failure**; the `FILEHDR PHDRS` idiom is mandatory (not just an auxv nicety as for Rust: `__init_tls` dereferences `AT_PHDR`). No `PT_TLS` — musl keeps `errno` in the pthread struct via `tpidr_el0`, so `libc.a` has no `.tdata`/`.tbss`. **The 4 KiB exec stack was measured sufficient (~2 KB worst chain) and was NOT grown** — but v1.2.6's `fmt_fp` allocates a **VLA** (~512 B for `%f`, **~7.4 KB for `%Lf`**), so a future C program printing a `long double` will overflow it and *no static frame scan will predict that*. `PM_EXEC` gained a name payload (`PM_EXEC_NAME_OFF`, reusing `EXEC_NAME_LEN`), PM's `EXEC_TARGET` is gone, and **init alternates `worker`/`hello`** (`EXEC_TARGETS`, worker **first** — `probe_pid` keys 5.5's verdict on the first child) so the exec-stack proof survives the C milestone; the target is chosen *before* the fork so both halves of the SENDREC agree. The boot marker is **`name=hello entry=` with no `target=` slot**: init's fork pool gives `hello` slot 15 stub-free but **16** with stubs, so a slot-keyed marker passes in one config and is vacuous in the other. **ABI freeze (D8): past this slice `Message` layout, call numbers, endpoints, and errnos change only via a deliberate ABI-bump PR touching both repos** — there is now C in another repository depending on all four. Since the port branch is **force-pushed** on rebase, a fork rebase and the `external/musl` bump must land in the **same PR**, or this repo pins an orphaned commit

Six syscalls suffice only because of startup facts that must be **re-verified, never assumed, on any musl bump** (all re-read against v1.2.6, recorded in the fork's `MINIXRS.md`): `__init_libc` early-returns past its `ppoll` when `AT_UID`/`AT_GID`/`AT_SECURE` are absent (they read 0); `__init_ssp(NULL)` derives the canary arithmetically; `__init_tp`'s only syscall is `set_tid_address` (`__set_thread_area` is `msr tpidr_el0` inline asm since v1.2.6) and it **walks `libc.auxv`**, so the auxv must stay `AT_NULL`-terminated; `__init_tls` uses static `builtin_tls` absent a `PT_TLS` (so no `mmap`) and walks 5.5's `AT_PHDR`/`AT_PHNUM`/`AT_PHENT`. **`tools/build-musl.sh`** builds an out-of-tree sysroot into `target/musl-sysroot` (the submodule work tree stays **pristine** — the `c-headers` job asserts a clean `git status`), keyed by a `.stamp` of submodule SHA + toolchain; `RANLIB` is **`llvm-ar s`**, because the pinned toolchain ships `llvm-ar` but **not** `llvm-ranlib`. It also runs the **real D7 errno *value* check** 5.0 deferred here — the opt-in POSIX block compiled against the fork's own `bits/errno.h` under `-nostdinc -isystem <sysroot>/include`; the CI `c-headers` job keeps only the hermetic stand-in check. `userland/hello` is **not a cargo crate** — `hello.c` + `hello.ld` compiled by clang and linked by `rust-lld` inside `kernel/build.rs::build_hello`, packed under proc_nr `-1` like `worker`. **The fallback presence-checks the SYSROOT (`.stamp`), not the submodule**, and packs the `worker` ELF *under the name* `hello` with a `cargo::warning` — checking the submodule would let a fresh clone trigger a multi-minute libc build from inside a build script. musl's `vfprintf` needs soft-float **binary128** builtins (`__multf3`/`__floatsitf`/…; aarch64 `long double` is IEEE quad) which musl's configure finds no library for: they come from **`compiler_builtins` as built by `-Zbuild-std` for `aarch64-unknown-minixrs`** — the *prebuilt* `aarch64-unknown-none` rlib in the rustup sysroot does **not** export the C-ABI names, so glob the nested target dir, never the sysroot. `hello.ld` is `worker/user.ld` plus what only a musl link brings — `.init`/`.fini` (they define the `_init`/`_fini` `crt1.c` passes to `__libc_start_main`), `.init_array`/`.fini_array` with bracketing symbols, `.got`, `.data.rel.ro` — because **an orphan section past the last `PT_LOAD` is a silent load failure**; the `FILEHDR PHDRS` idiom is mandatory (not just an auxv nicety as for Rust: `__init_tls` dereferences `AT_PHDR`). No `PT_TLS` — musl keeps `errno` in the pthread struct via `tpidr_el0`, so `libc.a` has no `.tdata`/`.tbss`. **The 4 KiB exec stack was measured sufficient (~2 KB worst chain) and was NOT grown** — but v1.2.6's `fmt_fp` allocates a **VLA** (~512 B for `%f`, **~7.4 KB for `%Lf`**), so a future C program printing a `long double` will overflow it and *no static frame scan will predict that*. `PM_EXEC` gained a name payload (`PM_EXEC_NAME_OFF`, reusing `EXEC_NAME_LEN`), PM's `EXEC_TARGET` is gone, and **init alternates `worker`/`hello`** (`EXEC_TARGETS`, worker **first** — `probe_pid` keys 5.5's verdict on the first child) so the exec-stack proof survives the C milestone; the target is chosen *before* the fork so both halves of the SENDREC agree. The boot marker is **`name=hello entry=` with no `target=` slot**: init's fork pool gives `hello` slot 15 stub-free but **16** with stubs, so a slot-keyed marker passes in one config and is vacuous in the other. **ABI freeze (D8): past this slice `Message` layout, call numbers, endpoints, and errnos change only via a deliberate ABI-bump PR touching both repos** — there is now C in another repository depending on all four. Since the port branch is **force-pushed** on rebase, a fork rebase and the `external/musl` bump must land in the **same PR**, or this repo pins an orphaned commit

attachment.snippet:
1	/*
2	 * minix.rs user-space linker script (aarch64 EL0 `hello` — the slice-5.6 C
3	 * milestone, linked against the musl fork).
4	 *
5	 * Derived from `userland/worker/user.ld`, and the parts they share are load-
6	 * bearing in exactly the same way: a static ET_EXEC ELF the kernel's minimal
7	 * loader (`kernel/src/boot_image/elf.rs`) maps segment-by-segment into a fresh
8	 * per-process AddrSpace, every PT_LOAD page-aligned in vaddr *and* file offset,
9	 * no dynamic sections or relocations, and the same 0x0010_0000 load base (safe
10	 * to share, because exec always builds its own per-process TTBR0).
11	 *
12	 * The FILEHDR PHDRS idiom on the text segment is MANDATORY, not cosmetic.
13	 * Without it lld's default aarch64 max-page-size (64 KiB) puts PT_LOAD #0 at
14	 * file offset 0x10000 and leaves `e_phoff` in an unmapped prefix — so SYS_EXEC
15	 * has no mapped VA to report as AT_PHDR, and musl's `__init_tls`, which walks
16	 * the program headers from exactly that pointer, would dereference nothing.
17	 * For a Rust binary that costs an auxv entry; here it is a fault at startup.
18	 *
19	 * What this script has to place that a Rust one does not, all of it arriving
20	 * from crti.o / crtn.o / libc.a:
21	 *
22	 *   .init / .fini              `_init` and `_fini`, which crt1.c hands to
23	 *                              __libc_start_main. Orphaned, they land outside
24	 *                              a PT_LOAD and the call jumps into nothing.
25	 *   .init_array / .fini_array  walked by __libc_start_init and libc_exit_fini.
26	 *                              The bracketing symbols are weak-hidden in musl,
27	 *                              so an undefined pair merely skips the walk —
28	 *                              but a section placed with no symbols would be
29	 *                              walked with garbage bounds. Define both.
30	 *   .got / .data.rel.ro        emitted even for a static non-PIE link.
31	 *
32	 * Every input section gets an explicit home. An orphan placed past the last
33	 * PT_LOAD is a SILENT load failure — the loader maps what the phdrs describe
34	 * and never sees it. Verify with:
35	 *   llvm-readobj --program-headers --elf-output-style=GNU target/hello/hello
36	 *
37	 * There is deliberately no PT_TLS: musl keeps errno in the pthread struct via
38	 * tpidr_el0 rather than in a __thread variable, so libc.a carries no .tdata or
39	 * .tbss and __init_tls uses its static builtin_tls. The rules below still catch
40	 * those sections so a future libc change surfaces as a link-time surprise
41	 * rather than a runtime one.
42	 */
43	
44	OUTPUT_FORMAT(elf64-littleaarch64)
45	OUTPUT_ARCH(aarch64)
46	ENTRY(_start)
47	
48	PHDRS {
49	    text   PT_LOAD FLAGS(5); /* R+X MUTATION */
50	    rodata PT_LOAD FLAGS(4); /* R   */
51	    data   PT_LOAD FLAGS(6); /* RW  */
52	    note   PT_NOTE FLAGS(4); /* minixrs identity note */
53	}
54	
55	SECTIONS {
56	    . = 0x00100000; /* MUTATION */
57	
58	    .text : ALIGN(4K) {
59	        KEEP(*(.text._start))
60	        *(.text .text.*)
61	    } :text
62	
63	    /* crti.o / crtn.o bracket these; _init and _fini live inside them. */
64	    .init : {
65	        KEEP(*(.init))
66	    } :text
67	
68	    .fini : {
69	        KEEP(*(.fini))
70	    } :text
71	
72	    . = ALIGN(4K);
73	    /*
74	     * minixrs identity note (tooling/docs/abi-note.md): first thing in the RO
75	     * segment, dual-assigned so it lands in the rodata PT_LOAD *and* its own
76	     * PT_NOTE phdr. KEEP() is mandatory — nothing references the section — and
77	     * this rule must stay ahead of the /DISCARD/ *(.note.*) rule below (first
78	     * match wins).
79	     *
80	     * For a C binary the note comes from crt1.o, where the fork emits it as a
81	     * .pushsection global asm, so every C program is branded with no opt-in.
82	     */
83	    .note.minixrs.ident : {
84	        KEEP(*(.note.minixrs.ident))
85	    } :rodata :note
86	
87	    .rodata : {
88	        *(.rodata .rodata.*)
89	    } :rodata
90	
91	    . = ALIGN(4K);
92	
93	    /*
94	     * Constructor/destructor arrays. PROVIDE_HIDDEN matches what musl declares
95	     * (weak hidden), and bracketing them here is what keeps the walk bounded.
96	     */
97	    .preinit_array : {
98	        PROVIDE_HIDDEN(__preinit_array_start = .);
99	        KEEP(*(.preinit_array))
100	        PROVIDE_HIDDEN(__preinit_array_end = .);
101	    } :data
102	
103	    .init_array : {
104	        PROVIDE_HIDDEN(__init_array_start = .);
105	        KEEP(*(SORT_BY_INIT_PRIORITY(.init_array.*)))
106	        KEEP(*(.init_array))
107	        PROVIDE_HIDDEN(__init_array_end = .);
108	    } :data
109	
110	    .fini_array : {
111	        PROVIDE_HIDDEN(__fini_array_start = .);
112	        KEEP(*(SORT_BY_INIT_PRIORITY(.fini_array.*)))
113	        KEEP(*(.fini_array))

content.text:
Implementation and verification are complete. The only thing left needs commits, which your auto-mode rule says to surface first.

**Verified end-to-end** — milestone A is real:
```
minix.rs hello: Hello from C!      ← printf → VFS → TTY, from C
minix.rs hello: errno ok           ← D7 errno identity, at runtime
minix.rs hello: iov ok match=1     ← two-iovec writev
```
63/63 boot markers pass in the default config; all 5.5 markers survive alongside the new ones; stub-free config clean; fmt, both kernel clippy gates, workspace clippy, and 8 test suites green.

**Five findings worth flagging** — four are places the plan's expectations didn't survive contact:

1. **The errno check was vacuous when first written.** macOS `sed` has no `\b`, so `CHECK_MACRO` kept the old spelling while CI/script defined the new one — the guarded block compiled **0** assertions. Now 40, and mutation-proven (`libc EDEADLK disagrees with kernel-shared error.rs`).
2. **The plan's `target=15 name=hello` marker would have failed CI.** `hello` is slot **16** with stubs, 15 only stub-free. Keyed on `name=hello entry=` instead.
3. **Mutation 2 initially proved nothing.** `hello` never produced two non-empty iovecs (musl's stdout starts *line*-buffered, so the first `printf` flushes and leaves the buffer empty). I restructured `hello.c` to set the case up deliberately; the mutation now hangs the program and drops all four markers.
4. **`llvm-ranlib` doesn't ship** with the pinned toolchain (`llvm-ar s` instead), and musl needed **quad-float builtins** — sourced from the `-Zbuild-std` `compiler_builtins`, since the prebuilt sysroot rlib doesn't export the C-ABI names. No LLVM build added.
5. **The 4 KiB exec stack was sufficient** (~2 KB measured) — §7's growth wasn't needed. But v1.2.6's `fmt_fp` uses a **VLA**: ~7.4 KB for `%Lf`. A future C program printing a `long double` will overflow it, and no static scan predicts it. Recorded in CLAUDE.md and the plan.

I also did the `minix-ipc/` → `minixrs-ipc/` rename you asked for (53 files, workspace green).

# musl-minixrs — the minix.rs libc fork

This is [musl libc](https://musl.libc.org/) with its Linux syscall ABI replaced
by [minix.rs](https://github.com/minixrs/minixrs) IPC. It exists so that
ordinary C programs — compiled with an unmodified clang, linked against an
almost-unmodified musl — run on a MINIX-style microkernel where every OS
service is a user-space server reached by message passing.

musl is MIT licensed; see `COPYRIGHT`. This fork adds nothing under a different
licence.

## Branch layout

| Branch | What it is |
|---|---|
| `main` | A **pristine mirror** of upstream `master`. Never commit to it. |
| `minixrs` | The port. Based on tag **`v1.2.6`** (2026-03-20). The default branch. |

`main` exists so the fork is diffable against upstream without a second remote.
Refresh it with:

```sh
git fetch upstream
git checkout main
git merge --ff-only upstream/master
```

The port branch is pinned to a **tag**, never to `main`'s head — a libc that
moves under you is not a base you can debug a kernel against. Moving to a new
release is a deliberate act:

```sh
git rebase --onto v1.2.7 v1.2.6 minixrs
git push --force-with-lease origin minixrs
```

Because the port branch is force-pushed, **the minix.rs submodule pin must be
bumped in the same PR as any rebase** (`external/musl` in the minixrs repo). A
rebase orphans the previously pinned SHA, and a submodule pointing at an
orphaned commit fails to clone rather than failing loudly at build time.

## Delta contract

The port is deliberately tiny, and staying tiny is a design goal rather than an
accident — every file that stays byte-identical to upstream is a file that
rebases for free onto the next release. **The entire minix.rs footprint is:**

| Path | What it does |
|---|---|
| `arch/aarch64/syscall_arch.h` | `__syscall0..6` call `__minixrs_syscall`; VDSO macros deleted |
| `src/minixrs/ipc.c` | The `svc #0` IPC trap |
| `src/minixrs/_syscall.c` | Linux syscall number → server IPC |
| `src/minixrs/minixrs_internal.h` | Shared declarations for the two above |
| `crt/crt1.c` | The 28-byte `.note.minixrs.ident` ELF brand |
| `MINIXRS.md` | This file |

Nothing else. `git diff v1.2.6 --stat` should show exactly two modified files
outside `src/minixrs/`.

**No Makefile change is needed** to build `src/minixrs/`: musl globs its source
directories (`SRC_DIRS = $(addprefix $(srcdir)/,src/* …)` in the `Makefile`), so
a new `src/<name>/` directory is picked up automatically. Verified against the
v1.2.6 tree.

`src/internal/syscall_ret.c` is **untouched on purpose**. It treats a return
value in `[-4095, -1]` as an errno, and minix.rs errno magnitudes are `1..=40`
and `>= 200` (phase-5 decision D7), so all of them land inside that window. The
POSIX block additionally uses the same values Linux and musl do, which is why
musl's stock `bits/errno.h` needs no edit either.

## The seam

musl's ~297 `__syscall` call sites are all unmodified. They still emit Linux
syscall numbers. `arch/aarch64/syscall_arch.h` is the one place that knows
better: instead of executing `svc` with the number in `x8`, every `__syscallN`
calls `__minixrs_syscall`, which switches on the Linux number and issues the
corresponding server round-trip.

Keeping that shape — rather than rewriting call sites — is what lets the other
~1900 source files stay identical to upstream.

The IPC trap ABI is fixed by the kernel's `trap.S` and reproduced exactly in
`src/minixrs/ipc.c`. It is the C twin of the Rust `minixrs-ipc` crate:

```
x0 = endpoint (also receives the result)
x1 = IPC primitive (SEND / RECEIVE / SENDREC / NOTIFY / SENDNB)
x2 = pointer to the 104-byte message
svc #0
```

### Implemented syscalls

| Linux syscall | minix.rs mapping |
|---|---|
| `writev` | one `VFS_WRITE` per iovec, counts summed; partial progress reported on a mid-loop error |
| `write` | one `VFS_WRITE` |
| `exit_group`, `exit` | `PM_EXIT` (does not return) |
| `set_tid_address` | constant tid `1` |
| `ioctl` | `-ENOTTY` |
| everything else | `-ENOSYS` |

`ioctl` returning `-ENOTTY` is load-bearing rather than merely harmless:
`__stdout_write` sets `f->lbf = -1` when `TIOCGWINSZ` fails, which makes stdout
**fully buffered**. `printf` output is then flushed by `exit()`'s
`__stdio_exit`, so the flush path is exercised by any program that prints.

`writev` is the one that carries stdio — `__stdio_write` always calls `writev`,
never `write`, and loops until the returned count equals what it asked for. The
count returned must therefore be exact; over-reporting makes musl believe a
flush completed that did not.

## Linux dependency inventory (re-derived against v1.2.6)

musl references **341 distinct `SYS_*` numbers** across 297 call sites. The port
implements six. That is viable only because of what the startup path does *not*
do — each of the following was re-read in the v1.2.6 source, not assumed:

| Fact | Consequence |
|---|---|
| `__init_libc` returns early when `AT_UID==AT_EUID && AT_GID==AT_EGID && !AT_SECURE` — all read `0` when absent from the auxv | the secure-mode branch, the **only** `ppoll`/`open` in startup, never runs |
| `__init_ssp(NULL)` (no `AT_RANDOM`) derives the canary as `&__stack_chk_guard * 1103515245` | no syscall |
| `__init_tp` issues exactly one syscall, `set_tid_address` | `__set_thread_area` is `msr tpidr_el0` inline asm on aarch64 (v1.2.6 replaced the `.s` file) |
| `__init_tls` uses the static `builtin_tls` when the program has no `PT_TLS` | no `mmap` |
| `__init_tls` walks `AT_PHDR` / `AT_PHNUM` / `AT_PHENT` | the kernel must supply them — minix.rs does, since slice 5.5 |
| `__set_thread_area` walks `libc.auxv` to mask SME hwcap bits | the auxv **must** be `AT_NULL`-terminated |

Tiers of what remains, roughly by distance:

- **Next up (minix.rs slice 5.8+):** `openat`, `read`, `close`, `lseek` — real
  file I/O, once there is a filesystem server. These are already referenced by
  code that links today; they simply answer `-ENOSYS`.
- **Needs kernel work:** `mmap`/`munmap`/`brk` (minix.rs has `VM_MMAP`/`VM_BRK`
  but no libc wiring), `futex` (no threads yet), signal delivery
  (`rt_sigaction` and friends — minix.rs signals default-terminate).
- **Wholly Linux, unlikely to ever be ported:** everything under `src/linux/`
  (`epoll`, `inotify`, `sendfile`, `prctl`, cgroup and namespace calls), plus
  `src/aio`, `src/mq`, and the netlink paths in `src/network`. These compile
  into `libc.a` and answer `-ENOSYS` if called; nothing links them in by
  accident.

## The ELF brand

Every minix.rs user-space binary carries a 28-byte `.note.minixrs.ident` note
(the normative spec is `docs/abi-note.md` in the minixrs tooling repo). The
kernel **refuses to load an unbranded ELF**.

The note is emitted from `crt/crt1.c` as a `.pushsection` global asm, so every C
binary gets it regardless of how it was linked, and no program has to opt in.
`crt1.o` is linked explicitly into every executable rather than pulled from an
archive, so — unlike a `libc.a` member — it can never be dropped by
archive-member selection.

Its bytes are identical to what the Rust `minixrs_abi_note::brand!()` macro
emits, so a C binary and a Rust one are indistinguishable to the verifier:

```
08 00 00 00              namesz = 8
08 00 00 00              descsz = 8
01 00 00 00              type   = NT_MINIXRS_IDENT
6d 69 6e 69 78 72 73 00  "minixrs\0"
01 00 00 00              abi_version = 1
00 00 00 00              flags = 0
```

A linker script consuming this libc must `KEEP()` the section and give it a
dedicated `PT_NOTE` at the start of the read-only `PT_LOAD`. Regressing the
brand fails the **minix.rs kernel build**, not the boot: `kernel/build.rs` runs
the same `scan_brand` check when it packs the boot archive.

## Building

The canonical build is `tools/build-musl.sh` in the minixrs repo, which drives
configure/make into a cached sysroot at `target/musl-sysroot`. To build by hand:

```sh
mkdir build && cd build
SR="$(rustc --print sysroot)"; AR=$(echo "$SR"/lib/rustlib/*/bin/llvm-ar)
../configure --target=aarch64-linux-musl --disable-shared \
  --prefix=/path/to/sysroot \
  CC="clang --target=aarch64-unknown-linux-musl" \
  AR="$AR" RANLIB="$AR s" \
  CFLAGS="-I/path/to/minixrs/target/gen-c-headers/include"
make && make install
```

Notes:

- Build **out of tree**. The minixrs repo vendors this as a submodule and its
  CI asserts a clean `git status`, so nothing may be written into the work tree.
- `RANLIB="$AR s"` rather than `llvm-ranlib`: the pinned Rust toolchain ships
  `llvm-ar` but **not** `llvm-ranlib`. `llvm-ar s` writes the archive index,
  which is all `ranlib` is for here.
- The `CFLAGS` `-I` is how `src/minixrs/*.c` finds `<minixrs/ipc.h>` under
  musl's `-nostdinc`. Those headers are generated by `cargo gen-c-headers` in
  the minixrs repo from the live Rust constants — they are a build artifact and
  are never committed to either repo.
- configure's linker probes all fail under Apple clang (its default linker is
  ld64). That is harmless: `--disable-shared` means only `libc.a` and the crt
  objects are produced, and consumers link with `rust-lld`.

All four review items are addressed and verified. Both configs still clean.

**#1 (`syscall_cp.s`) — valid, and I confirmed the mechanism precisely.** It's latent, not active, but the reason matters: `src/thread/__syscall_cp.c` supplies a *weak* `__syscall_cp_c` routing through the port, while `pthread_cancel.c` supplies a *strong* one calling `__syscall_cp_asm`. Whichever TU gets linked silently decides whether `read`/`write`/`open`/`close` take the raw Linux `svc`. `hello` got the safe path by accident of linkage.

Fixed by forwarding `__syscall_cp_asm` to `__minixrs_syscall` (arg registers shifted down one), keeping `__cp_begin`/`__cp_end`/`__cp_cancel` intact. Proven by linking a program that *does* reference `pthread_cancel`:

```
__syscall_cp_asm:  mov x0,x1 … mov x6,x7
                   b  <__minixrs_syscall>     ← was: svc 0
```

That audit turned up something the review didn't mention: a threaded link still contains raw Linux `svc` in `__restore_rt`, `__clone`, and `__unmapself`. Those need a threading/signal model minix.rs doesn't have, so I recorded them in `MINIXRS.md` with the condition that makes each reachable, plus the one-liner to audit any binary. A single-threaded C program must show exactly one `svc`, in `__minixrs_ipc` — `hello` does.

**#2–#4** — all valid, all applied: `hidden` declaration moved into `minixrs_internal.h` so the definition sees it (it was getting default visibility because `_syscall.c` includes the *public* `<sys/syscall.h>`); `IOV_MAX`/negative-count → `EINVAL` and null-iov → `EFAULT`; explicit `__builtin_unreachable()` after the `_Noreturn` exit arm.

One judgement call worth surfacing: the tail-branch means `__cp_end` is no longer reached, so the cancellation *window* no longer brackets the trap. === syscalls.md 260-290 ===
## Generated C headers

The ABI above is described to C by headers **generated from the live Rust
constants** and never committed (phase-5 decision D8):

| Header | Contents |
|--------|----------|
| `minix/ipc.h` | the `message` struct, endpoint packing macros, IPC primitives |
| `minix/com.h` | process numbers and the boot endpoints derived from them |
| `minix/callnr.h` | kernel-call numbers and the server request bands |
| `minix/errno.h` | the MINIX 200-band errnos; an opt-in check on the C library's POSIX ones |

```sh
cargo gen-c-headers          # -> target/gen-c-headers/
```

Every value comes from `kernel-shared`, and the headers carry `_Static_assert`s
pinning the `message` layout and the endpoint encode/decode against it — so an
ABI change on the Rust side fails to compile on the C side rather than silently
corrupting IPC. See [Build & CI](../build.md#generated-c-headers).

## MINIX 3 source references

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `include/minix/callnr.h` | PM and VFS call numbers |
| `include/minix/com.h` | Kernel-call numbers and IPC constants |
| `lib/libc/sys/syscall.c` | User-space `_syscall()` |
| `lib/libsys/kernel_call.c` | Server-side `_kernel_call()` |

=== ipc/overview.md 38-46 ===

> **Note on the "64-bit MINIX 3" reference.** MINIX 3 only ever shipped as a
> 32-bit operating system (i386, and later 32-bit ARM on the BeagleBone). Its
> source tree does carry x86_64 ABI definitions — including the `__x86_64__`
> branch of `include/minix/ipc.h` that fixes `sizeof(message) == 104` — but the
> upstream project never released a working 64-bit MINIX 3. A **functioning
> 64-bit MINIX 3 prototype was a personal effort by this project's author (Kevin
> Barnard), separate from the upstream MINIX 3 project**. minix.rs takes that
> 104-byte layout as its ABI reference point, but is itself a clean, 64-bit-only

| IPC dispatch | `kernel/proc.c` | `do_ipc`, `do_sync_ipc` |
| Blocking send / receive | `kernel/proc.c` | `mini_send`, `mini_receive` |
| Notification / async send | `kernel/proc.c` | `mini_notify`, `mini_senda` |
| Deadlock detection | `kernel/proc.c` | `deadlock` |
| Process / privilege tables | `kernel/proc.h`, `priv.h` | `struct proc`, `struct priv` |
| Message / IPC constants | `include/minix/ipc.h`, `ipcconst.h` | `message`, `SEND`, … |

content.content:
cargo gen-c-headers                 # -> target/gen-c-headers/
cargo gen-c-headers /some/sysroot   # explicit output directory
cargo gen-c-headers --stdout        # eyeball the output
```

It emits `include/minix/{ipc,com,callnr,errno}.h`, plus two artifacts that make
the CI gate real: `abi-selftest.c` — a header is never a translation unit on its
own, so without a `.c` file none of the generated `_Static_assert`s would ever
fire — and `abi-check/errno.h`, a CI-only stand-in for the C library's
`<errno.h>`.

Two things the headers are careful about:

- **`_PROC_NR` vs `_EP`.** Every process gets both. minix.rs sign-extends the
  endpoint proc field instead of using MINIX 3's offset bias, so for the kernel
  tasks the boot endpoint is *not* the process number (`SYSTEM_PROC_NR` is −2,
  `SYSTEM_EP` is 32766). Naming a task by its `_PROC_NR` in an IPC call is a bug,
  and the header asserts the C decode macro against the Rust-computed endpoints.
- **The POSIX errno block is asserted, never defined.** minix.rs adopts musl's
  numbering verbatim, so those values must come from the C library's own
  `<errno.h>`; `minix/errno.h` defines only the MINIX 200-band and puts the
  POSIX checks behind `MINIX_ABI_CHECK_POSIX_ERRNO`, which the musl build
  defines. See [System Calls & ABI](reference/syscalls.md).

input.old_string:
MUSL_SHA=$(git -C "$MUSL_SRC" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)

input.new_string:
MUSL_SHA=$(git -C "$MUSL_SRC" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)

# Hash portably. macOS ships `shasum` (perl) but no `sha256sum`; Linux ships
# `sha256sum` (coreutils) and usually but not always `shasum`. `cksum` is in
# POSIX and is the last resort -- it is a weak checksum, but this only has to
# detect a toolchain CHANGE, not resist an adversary.
#
# Failing loudly matters: a hash command that printed nothing would make every
# stamp compare equal, and the sysroot would silently never rebuild.
hash_stdin() {
	if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
		sha256sum
	elif command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
		shasum -a 256
	elif command -v openssl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
		openssl dgst -sha256 | sed 's/.*= //'
	else
		cksum
	fi
}

TOOLCHAIN_ID=$(
	{ cat "$ROOT/rust-toolchain.toml" 2>/dev/null || true; clang --version | head -1; } \
		| hash_stdin | cut -d' ' -f1
)
if [ -z "$TOOLCHAIN_ID" ]; then
	echo "error: could not hash the toolchain identity (no sha256sum/shasum/openssl/cksum?)" >&2
	exit 1
fi
WANT="musl=$MUSL_SHA toolchain=$TOOLCHAIN_ID"

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
# Copyright (c) 2025-2026 Kevin Barnard and minix.rs Contributors
#
# Build the musl fork (external/musl) into a cached sysroot at
# target/musl-sysroot (phase-5 decision D10).
#
# Everything this writes lives under target/. The submodule work tree is left
# PRISTINE -- the c-headers CI job asserts a clean `git status`, and a build
# that dirties a submodule would fail it. musl supports out-of-tree builds, so
# the object tree goes to target/musl-build.
#
# Rebuilds are skipped when target/musl-sysroot/.stamp already matches the
# submodule SHA and the toolchain. Pass --force to rebuild anyway.
#
# Environment:
#   MUSL_SRC   musl source tree (default: external/musl). Point this at a local
#              fork checkout to test a port change before bumping the submodule.

set -eu

ROOT=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")/.." && pwd)
MUSL_SRC=${MUSL_SRC:-$ROOT/external/musl}
SYSROOT=$ROOT/target/musl-sysroot
BUILD=$ROOT/target/musl-build
HDRS=$ROOT/target/gen-c-headers
STAMP=$SYSROOT/.stamp

FORCE=0
[ "${1:-}" = "--force" ] && FORCE=1

if [ ! -f "$MUSL_SRC/configure" ]; then
	echo "error: no musl source at $MUSL_SRC" >&2
	echo "       run: git submodule update --init --recursive" >&2
	exit 1
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Toolchain. Both binutils replacements ship with the pinned Rust nightly, so
# there is no Homebrew LLVM dependency.
#
# RANLIB is `llvm-ar s`, not llvm-ranlib: the toolchain ships llvm-ar but NOT
# llvm-ranlib, and `llvm-ar s` writes the archive index, which is all ranlib
# does here.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
SR=$(rustc --print sysroot)
AR=$(echo "$SR"/lib/rustlib/*/bin/llvm-ar)
if [ ! -x "$AR" ]; then
	echo "error: llvm-ar not found under $SR/lib/rustlib/*/bin" >&2
	exit 1
fi
CC="clang --target=aarch64-unknown-linux-musl"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Freshness. The stamp keys on the exact musl commit plus the toolchain, so a
# submodule bump or a nightly bump both invalidate it. CI uses the same value
# as its cache key.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
MUSL_SHA=$(git -C "$MUSL_SRC" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
TOOLCHAIN_ID=$(
	{ cat "$ROOT/rust-toolchain.toml" 2>/dev/null || true; clang --version | head -1; } \
		| shasum | cut -d' ' -f1
)
WANT="musl=$MUSL_SHA toolchain=$TOOLCHAIN_ID"

if [ "$FORCE" -eq 0 ] && [ -f "$STAMP" ] && [ -f "$SYSROOT/lib/libc.a" ]; then
	if [ "$(cat "$STAMP")" = "$WANT" ]; then
		echo "musl sysroot up to date ($SYSROOT)"
		exit 0
	fi
fi

echo "building musl fork -> $SYSROOT"
echo "  source:    $MUSL_SRC ($MUSL_SHA)"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The generated ABI headers come first: src/minixrs/*.c includes <minixrs/ipc.h>
# and friends, and musl compiles its own sources with -nostdinc, so the only way
# in is an explicit -I in CFLAGS.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
( cd "$ROOT" && cargo gen-c-headers >/dev/null )

rm -rf "$BUILD" "$SYSROOT"
mkdir -p "$BUILD"

( cd "$BUILD" && "$MUSL_SRC/configure" \
	--target=aarch64-linux-musl \
	--prefix="$SYSROOT" \
	--disable-shared \
	CC="$CC" \
	AR="$AR" \
	RANLIB="$AR s" \
	CFLAGS="-I$HDRS/include" >/dev/null )

# configure's linker probes all fail under a Darwin-hosted clang (its default
# linker is ld64). Harmless: --disable-shared means only libc.a and the crt
# objects are built, and consumers link with rust-lld.

make -C "$BUILD" -j"$(getconf _NPROCESSORS_ONLN 2>/dev/null || echo 4)" >/dev/null
make -C "$BUILD" install >/dev/null

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Install the generated minix.rs ABI headers alongside musl's own, so a C
# program compiles against one -isystem path. They are copied into the SYSROOT,
# never into the submodule work tree.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
mkdir -p "$SYSROOT/include/minixrs"
cp "$HDRS"/include/minixrs/*.h "$SYSROOT/include/minixrs/"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The D7 errno check, for real.
#
# Slice 5.0 deferred this to 5.6 because CI had no musl sysroot: until now the
# opt-in POSIX block was only ever compiled against a generated stand-in, which
# proves macro spellings but not values. Here it compiles against the FORK'S OWN
# bits/errno.h in the installed sysroot, so a POSIX errno whose value drifted
# from musl's is a build failure.
#
# -nostdinc + -isystem "$SYSROOT/include" is what makes it honest: the host libc
# cannot creep in (Darwin EDEADLK is 11, not 35).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo "  checking:  POSIX errno values against the fork's bits/errno.h"
clang -std=c11 -pedantic-errors -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fsyntax-only \
	--target=aarch64-unknown-linux-musl \
	-nostdinc -isystem "$SYSROOT/include" \
	-DMINIXRS_ABI_CHECK_POSIX_ERRNO \
	"$HDRS/abi-selftest.c"

printf '%s' "$WANT" > "$STAMP"
echo "musl sysroot ready ($SYSROOT)"

cd /Users/kevinbarnard/src/minixrs-forks/musl-minixrs && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
slice 5.6a: port musl to minix.rs IPC (aarch64)

Replace musl's Linux syscall ABI with minix.rs message passing, so ordinary C
compiled against this libc runs on a MINIX-style microkernel where every OS
service is a user-space server.

The delta is deliberately tiny -- every file that stays byte-identical to
upstream rebases for free onto the next release:

  arch/aarch64/syscall_arch.h      __syscall0..6 -> __minixrs_syscall; VDSO gone
  src/thread/aarch64/syscall_cp.s  __syscall_cp_asm forwards to the port
  src/minixrs/ipc.c                the svc #0 IPC trap
  src/minixrs/_syscall.c           Linux syscall number -> server IPC
  src/minixrs/minixrs_internal.h   shared declarations
  crt/crt1.c                       the .note.minixrs.ident ELF brand
  MINIXRS.md                       branch + delta contracts, Linux inventory

musl's ~297 __syscall call sites are untouched; that seam is what lets the
other ~1900 source files stay identical. src/minixrs/ needs no Makefile edit --
musl globs src/*/. syscall_ret.c is untouched because minix.rs errno magnitudes
(1..=40 and >=200) all sit inside its > -4096UL window.

Mapped: writev/write -> VFS_WRITE, exit/exit_group -> PM_EXIT, set_tid_address
-> 1, ioctl -> -ENOTTY, everything else -ENOSYS. The ioctl answer is
load-bearing: it makes __stdout_write set f->lbf = -1, so stdout is fully
buffered and printf is flushed by exit()'s __stdio_exit.

syscall_cp.s is in the delta because redirecting syscall_arch.h alone is not
enough. Cancellable syscalls (read/write/open/close) reach __syscall_cp, and
which implementation that resolves to is decided by LINKAGE: __syscall_cp.c
supplies a weak __syscall_cp_c routing through the port, pthread_cancel.c a
strong one calling __syscall_cp_asm, which upstream ends in a bare `svc 0`. A
program touching pthread_cancel would silently route every cancellable syscall
onto a raw Linux trap -- which on minix.rs is read as an endpoint, a primitive
and a message pointer. It now forwards to __minixrs_syscall regardless.

Three asm files still hold a raw Linux svc (__restore_rt, __clone,
__unmapself). None is reachable without threads or signal delivery, and porting
them means inventing semantics minix.rs does not have yet, so MINIXRS.md
records them with the condition that makes each reachable.

Verified: a C hello world exec'd from the minix.rs boot archive reaches serial
through printf -> VFS -> TTY; write(3,...) returns -1/EBADF; the two-iovec
writev path is exercised and mutation-tested. A single-threaded binary contains
exactly one svc, in __minixrs_ipc.

Based on upstream v1.2.6.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

Replaces musl's Linux syscall ABI with minix.rs message passing, so ordinary C
compiled against this libc runs on the microkernel. Based on upstream **v1.2.6**.

Paired with the minix.rs-side PR that vendors this branch as `external/musl`.

## Delta contract

The whole minix.rs footprint, and nothing else:

| Path | What it does |
|---|---|
| `arch/aarch64/syscall_arch.h` | `__syscall0..6` call `__minixrs_syscall`; VDSO macros deleted |
| `src/thread/aarch64/syscall_cp.s` | `__syscall_cp_asm` forwards to the port instead of `svc` |
| `src/minixrs/ipc.c` | the `svc #0` IPC trap |
| `src/minixrs/_syscall.c` | Linux syscall number → server IPC |
| `src/minixrs/minixrs_internal.h` | shared declarations |
| `crt/crt1.c` | the 28-byte `.note.minixrs.ident` ELF brand |
| `MINIXRS.md` | branch + delta contracts, Linux dependency inventory |

musl's ~297 `__syscall` call sites are untouched — that seam is what lets the
other ~1900 files stay byte-identical and rebase for free. `src/minixrs/` needs
no Makefile edit (musl globs `src/*/`), and `syscall_ret.c` is untouched because
minix.rs errno magnitudes (`1..=40`, `>=200`) all sit inside its `> -4096UL`
window.

## Mapped syscalls

`writev`/`write` → `VFS_WRITE`, `exit`/`exit_group` → `PM_EXIT`,
`set_tid_address` → `1`, `ioctl` → `-ENOTTY`, everything else `-ENOSYS`.

`ioctl` returning `-ENOTTY` is load-bearing, not merely harmless: it makes
`__stdout_write` set `f->lbf = -1`, so stdout is fully buffered and `printf` is
flushed by `exit()`'s `__stdio_exit`.

Six syscalls suffice only because of startup facts re-derived against v1.2.6
(not assumed) and recorded in `MINIXRS.md` — `__init_libc`'s early return past
its `ppoll`, `__init_ssp(NULL)`, `__init_tp`'s single `set_tid_address`, and
`__init_tls` falling back to `builtin_tls`.

## Why `syscall_cp.s` is in the delta

Redirecting `syscall_arch.h` alone is not enough. Cancellable syscalls
(`read`, `write`, `open`, `close`) reach `__syscall_cp`, and **which
implementation that resolves to is decided by linkage**:

- `src/thread/__syscall_cp.c` → **weak** `__syscall_cp_c`, routes through the port
- `src/thread/pthread_cancel.c` → **strong** one, calls `__syscall_cp_asm`, which
  upstream ends in a bare `svc 0`

So a program that never touches `pthread_cancel` got the safe path *by accident*;
one that does would silently route every cancellable syscall onto a raw Linux
trap — read by minix.rs as an endpoint, a primitive and a message pointer.
`__syscall_cp_asm` now forwards to `__minixrs_syscall` regardless. Verified by
linking a program that references `pthread_cancel` and disassembling.

Cancellation is a no-op (no threads yet); `__cp_begin`/`__cp_end`/`__cp_cancel`
are preserved. The tail branch means the cancel *window* no longer brackets the
trap — stated as a limitation in the file rather than left to be discovered.

## Linux traps that deliberately remain

`__restore_rt`, `__clone`, `__unmapself` still contain a raw `svc`. None is
reachable without threads or signal delivery, and porting them means inventing
semantics minix.rs does not have. `MINIXRS.md` records each with the condition
that makes it reachable, plus a one-liner to audit any binary — a
single-threaded C program must show exactly one `svc`, in `__minixrs_ipc`.

## Verification

A C hello world exec'd from the minix.rs boot archive reaches serial through
`printf` → VFS → TTY; `write(3, …)` returns `-1`/`EBADF`; the two-iovec `writev`
path is exercised. Mutation-tested (apply, watch the named marker move, revert):

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| drop the `crt1.c` brand block | kernel **build** fails at `pack_mxbi`'s `scan_brand` |
| `writev` handles one iovec | `__stdio_write` spins; all four hello markers vanish |
| clamp the negative VFS reply to 0 | `errno ok` → 0, forbidden `errno FAIL` fires |

lines: - **The exec initial stack — SysV frame, auxv, and a marker that proved nothing (slice 5.5, D13):** `SYS_EXEC` no longer just points `sp_el0` at the stack page top — it builds the **Linux/SysV initial frame** there first (`[argc][argv…][NULL][envp…][NULL][auxv pairs][AT_NULL]` then the NUL-terminated name, padded so `sp` is 16-aligned; `argc = 1`, empty envp) so musl's crt/`__libc_start_main`/`__init_tls` run **unpatched** — the standing keep-the-musl-diff-minimal principle only holds if the *kernel* supplies the frame. The byte layout lives in `kernel-shared/src/execstack.rs` (`build_initial_stack`, pure, zero `unsafe`, host-tested — the `user_va_ok`/`page_chunks` carve-out, since the kernel crate has no `#[cfg(test)]`); `do_exec` stages it in a `[u8; INITIAL_STACK_MAX]` **kernel-stack** buffer and installs it with 5.1's `copy_to_user_as`, which is address-space-independent by design, so no new copy machinery and the TTBR0 need not be installed. Both frame failures (`None` → `E2BIG`, copy error → `ENOMEM`) run `do_exit::teardown_addrspace` on the **fresh** image and return **before** the point of no return, extending `load_exec_image`'s leave-the-target-on-its-old-image invariant rather than weakening it. `elf::load_into` now returns a `LoadedElf { entry, phdr_va: Option<u64>, phnum, phentsize }`, `phdr_va` computed in the existing segment loop from the first `PT_LOAD` whose *file* range covers `[e_phoff, e_phoff + phnum*phentsize)`; `ExecImage` carries the three through. Auxv order is **fixed by the caller** (`AT_PHDR`, `AT_PHNUM`, `AT_PHENT`, `AT_PAGESZ`), not Linux's incidental order, so the trace and tests are deterministic. The `AT_*` values are the Linux/SysV ones and are deliberately **not** emitted by `gen-c-headers` — musl defines them itself. **`AT_PHDR` needs a linker-script opt-in, and the plan's "when the first PT_LOAD covers the ELF header" was otherwise *never* true:** lld's default aarch64 `max-page-size` (64 KiB) puts PT_LOAD #0 at file offset `0x10000`, leaving `e_phoff = 64` in an unmapped prefix, so a reported VA would fault `__init_tls`. `userland/worker/user.ld` therefore takes the `FILEHDR PHDRS` idiom (`text PT_LOAD FILEHDR PHDRS FLAGS(5)` + `. = <base> + SIZEOF_HEADERS`), giving PT_LOAD #0 at offset `0x0` / vaddr `0x100000` — both still page-aligned, so the loader's strict checks are untouched; only the entry moves one page up. **Server `user.ld`s stay unchanged** (boot-loaded images keep `sp = SERVER_STACK_VA + PAGE_SIZE` and never read an auxv). Any new exec'able binary that wants `AT_PHDR` must copy that idiom and be re-checked with `llvm-readobj --program-headers`. **EL0 is where the frame is proved:** `[exec] argc=1 envc=0 auxv=4 sp=0x` only says the kernel *thinks* it wrote one, so `worker` reads its real `sp` and validates the frame (alignment, argc, the `argv[0]` bytes through the stored pointer, both NULLs, `AT_PAGESZ`, and a phdr that reads back as `PT_LOAD` at the link base), returning `0` or the **1-based number of the first failing check**. That is what its `_start` is `#[unsafe(naked)]` + `naked_asm!("mov x0, sp", "b {main}")` for — a prologue could perturb `sp`, and taking the value in `x0` from the kernel would prove nothing about `SP_EL0`; the `#[cfg(all(not(test), target_arch = "aarch64"))]` split with a plain `main(0)` fallback is `minixrs-ipc`'s exact pattern, needed because CI's blocking clippy runs on x86_64 (the fallback must still *call* `main`, or it is dead code under `-D warnings`). The verdict rides out as the **exit status**, not a console line — worker runs once per init fork cycle — with a direct `stack FAIL` write to fd 2 as backup for the case where the status path is what broke. **The trap worth remembering: PM's `mproc::seed` parents the demo stubs to init, and stub D is SIGSEGV'd on purpose early in boot, so init's *first* `wait()` reaps that zombie (status 0), not a child it forked.** A marker keyed on "the first reap" printed `exec stack ok` beside 81 `worker: stack FAIL` lines under the argc mutation — vacuous, and *only* under default features, since `--no-default-features` has no stubs and its first reap really is the forked child. Key any reap-derived marker on the child's **pid** (`alloc_pid` never returns 0, so 0 is the "not yet" sentinel), and treat "a marker can be right in one feature config and prove nothing in the other" as the general lesson: mutation-test in the config that has the stubs. **The same trap has a second mouth:** `mproc::handle_kill_in` zombifies a *signalled* process without touching `exit_status`, so a probe that died before reporting is reaped with status 0 — and `validate` dereferences pointers out of the frame, so a bad enough frame faults it into VM's SIGSEGV arm, which prints no `!!! EL0 data abort` for the forbidden list to catch. Hence the pass is the positive sentinel `execstack::EXEC_STACK_PROBE_PASS` (`0x5A`) and status 0 prints `FAIL no-verdict`. General rule for any probe reporting through an exit status: **encode the pass, never the absence of a failure**

-- **C on minix.rs — the musl port, the sysroot, and the ABI freeze (slice 5.6, milestone A):** the libc is a **git submodule at `external/musl`** → `minixrs/musl-minixrs`, tracking branch **`minixrs`** (the port; `main` is a pristine upstream mirror with nothing on it), based on tag **`v1.2.6`**. The old `KevinBarnard/musl-minix` is archived and nothing was carried over. The fork's whole delta is `arch/aarch64/syscall_arch.h` + `src/minixrs/` + a brand block in `crt/crt1.c` + `MINIXRS.md`, and staying that small is the design goal — **musl globs `src/*/`, so `src/minixrs/` needs no Makefile edit**. slice 5.6: musl port — the first C program on minix.rs (milestone A)

A C program compiled against the musl fork runs on minix.rs, exec'd from the
boot archive, with printf reaching serial through VFS -> TTY:

  minix.rs hello: Hello from C!
  minix.rs hello: errno ok
  minix.rs hello: iov ok match=1

Nothing in hello.c is minix.rs-specific -- it is plain C against plain
<stdio.h>. It works because the libc underneath was ported, not the program.

Vendoring: external/musl is a submodule of minixrs/musl-minixrs (branch
`minixrs`, based on upstream v1.2.6). tools/build-musl.sh builds an out-of-tree
sysroot into target/musl-sysroot, keyed by a .stamp of submodule SHA +
toolchain, and leaves the submodule work tree pristine. It also runs the REAL
D7 errno *value* check that slice 5.0 deferred to here: the opt-in POSIX block
compiled against the fork's own bits/errno.h. Mutation-verified -- swapping
EDEADLK/ENAMETOOLONG fails the build.

userland/hello is not a cargo crate: hello.c + hello.ld compiled by clang and
linked by rust-lld inside kernel/build.rs, packed under proc_nr -1 like worker.
hello.ld adds what only a musl link brings -- .init/.fini, .init_array/
.fini_array with bracketing symbols, .got, .data.rel.ro -- because an orphan
section past the last PT_LOAD is a silent load failure. Quad-float builtins
(__multf3 etc.) come from compiler_builtins as built by -Zbuild-std; the
prebuilt aarch64-unknown-none rlib does not export the C ABI names.

PM_EXEC gains a name payload (PM_EXEC_NAME_OFF); PM's hardcoded EXEC_TARGET is
gone and init alternates worker/hello. Alternating rather than switching is
deliberate: retiring worker would have taken slice 5.5's exec-ABI proof with it.
Reading the name uses a new host-tested server-rt::payload::rd_name.

Naming: `minix` -> `minixrs` across the generated C surface (include/minixrs/,
_MINIXRS_OFFSETOF, MINIXRS_ABI_CHECK_POSIX_ERRNO) since this is the ABI freeze
and it was the last cheap moment. Prose citing MINIX 3's own headers is left
alone. The minix-ipc/ directory is renamed minixrs-ipc/ to match its package.

Two traps found by exercising rather than reading:

  * The errno check was VACUOUS as first written -- macOS sed has no \b, so
    CHECK_MACRO kept its old spelling while CI defined the new one and the
    guarded block compiled zero assertions. Now 40.
  * The worker-as-hello fallback made a FORBIDDEN marker fire: worker validated
    argv[0] against a hardcoded b"worker", so a missing sysroot printed
    `worker: stack FAIL` -- an absent optional dependency indistinguishable from
    a broken exec ABI. ARGV0_NAMES is now the set {worker, hello}.

Note for later: v1.2.6's fmt_fp uses a VLA -- ~512 B for %f but ~7.4 KB for
%Lf -- so a future C program printing a long double will overflow it, and no
static frame scan predicts that.

CI: qemu-smoke checks out submodules recursively and builds the sysroot before
the kernel, cached on the submodule's resolved commit (not a tracked file --
the port branch is force-pushed on rebase).

Declares the ABI freeze (D8): Message layout, call numbers, endpoints and
errnos now change only via a deliberate ABI-bump PR touching both repos.

Verified: 63/63 boot markers in the default config, all 5.5 markers intact,
stub-free config clean, fallback config clean, fmt + both kernel clippy gates +
workspace clippy + 10 test suites green.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

content.text:
Both PRs are open and CI is running; I'll report as checks land.

**Delivered — Phase 5 milestone A:**
- **[minixrs/musl-minixrs#1](https://github.com/minixrs/musl-minixrs/pull/1)** — the port (7 files, based on upstream v1.2.6)
- **[minixrs/minixrs#47](https://github.com/minixrs/minixrs/pull/47)** — the minix.rs side (61 files)

Neither is merged. The fork's `minixrs` branch is the PR base; merging #1 with a regular merge preserves `f1db256f`, which is what #47's submodule pins.

**Two defects that only surfaced by running things, not reading them:**

1. **The D7 errno check was vacuous when I first wrote it.** macOS `sed` has no `\b`, so `CHECK_MACRO` kept its old spelling while CI and the script defined the new one — the guarded block compiled **zero** assertions and reported success. Now 40, mutation-proven against musl's real `bits/errno.h`.
2. **The worker-as-hello fallback tripped a *forbidden* marker.** `worker` validates `argv[0]` against the exact bytes the kernel wrote and hardcoded `b"worker"`, so a missing sysroot printed `worker: stack FAIL` — an absent optional dependency looking identical to a broken exec ABI. Both Grok reviews and my own reading passed over the name-level substitution; only booting that config caught it. `ARGV0_NAMES` is now `{worker, hello}`.

**Deviations from the plan worth your attention:**
- The plan's marker `target=15 name=hello` would have **failed CI** — `hello` is slot 16 with stubs. Keyed on `name=hello entry=` instead.
- The 4 KiB exec stack was measured sufficient (~2 KB) and **not** grown. But v1.2.6's `fmt_fp` is a VLA: ~7.4 KB for `%Lf`. The next C program that prints a `long double` will overflow it, and no static scan predicts that — recorded in CLAUDE.md and the plan.
- `llvm-ranlib` doesn't ship with the toolchain (`llvm-ar s`), and quad-float builtins had to come from the `-Zbuild-std` `compiler_builtins` rather than the prebuilt rlib.

**One item I did not touch:** the tooling repo (`~/src/tooling`) has stale references your cross-repo rule says belong in a separate session — `scripts/export-patches.sh:14,49` still default `MINIXRS_MUSL_BASE` to `v1.2.5`, and `docs/roadmap.md:27,59` still say phase 5 is at slice 5.3 with P3 blocked on 5.4/5.5/5.6.
